optionChallenges.claimRepresented: Perform the remaining minute of inference synchronously before acknowledging the batch.
optionChallenges.whyIncorrectInContext: The endpoint has already spent 12 seconds; adding another minute exceeds Event Grid’s documented 30-second response wait. Earlier completion of two elements does not extend the batch response window.
optionChallenges.couldBeCorrectWhen: A handler can finish synchronously and acknowledge successfully when the entire batch completes within the response window.
optionChallenges.evidenceSummary: The full unit distinguishes the 30-second endpoint wait from complete processing and requires a success response for the whole batch.

optionChallenges.claimRepresented: Durably enqueue the unfinished job before returning a successful 202 for the batch.
optionChallenges.whyIncorrectInContext: Not incorrect: confirmed queue acceptance takes two seconds, keeping elapsed time at about 14 seconds. The two completed jobs already have durable results, and the queue/worker now owns the remaining job before whole-batch acknowledgement.
optionChallenges.couldBeCorrectWhen: A successful durable handoff before the HTTP deadline permits asynchronous acknowledgement. If the queue did not accept the job, starting a send alone would not justify the same success response.
optionChallenges.evidenceSummary: Event Grid treats 202 as successful asynchronous acceptance; Service Bus provides durable producer-consumer decoupling. Reliability sections preserve acknowledgement boundaries rather than promising exactly-once external effects.

optionChallenges.claimRepresented: Return a transient 503 failure and request another delivery of the whole batch.
optionChallenges.whyIncorrectInContext: 503 takes the retry path and the batching contract retries the whole delivery, violating the instruction not to ask Event Grid to replay the batch.
optionChallenges.couldBeCorrectWhen: Return 503 when durable acceptance fails or the endpoint cannot accept the batch and whole-batch retry is the desired recovery path.
optionChallenges.evidenceSummary: The delivery unit explicitly recommends 503 for transient inability to process and describes all-or-none acknowledgement for output batches.

challenges.scope: The reviewed boundary is one Basic Event Grid webhook delivery containing three jobs, then durable queue ownership for only unfinished work. HTTP batch acknowledgement cannot select just the finished elements.
challenges.plan: Basic webhook output batching is specified. Namespace pull-delivery contracts, unrelated premium throughput promises and unapproved Durable Functions capabilities are not used.
challenges.role: The queue can durably accept the job and a worker can process it, so missing send/receive authorization is not silently supplied. No role selection is asked.
challenges.preconditions: The two completed jobs are durable, the pending job has a supplied duration, and enqueue succeeds before response. These facts exclude volatile background work as an equivalent key.
challenges.featureStatus: The scenario uses ordinary documented 202/503 push-delivery and queue behavior, not a Preview SDK binding. Baseline claim scope does not establish credential GA.
challenges.sourceChanges: All three full source bodies were freshly reread, including explicit exceptions to broad retry wording. Their original MCP retrieval and source-review snapshots are preserved.
challenges.stemSufficiency: I recomputed 12+60 and 12+2 and checked the complete batch contract. A failed enqueue would change the suitable response, but the current successful-acceptance premise is explicit.
challenges.explanationBounds: The key avoids asking for a retry; it does not promise Event Grid can never deliver duplicates. The source-backed handoff does not create an atomic cross-service transaction.
challenges.reasoningDepth: The corrected Intermediate architecture-design label describes a modest actual placement of processing and durable responsibility under a response constraint. No Advanced or Expert credit is warranted.
challenges.answerClues: The correct option is somewhat longer and the feasible handoff is strongly supplied. The two alternatives remain real documented plans but receive a plausibility deduction. Webhook/batch pronouns are clear.

rubricReasons.alignment: The exact current Event Grid workflow subskill includes retries and service integration; placing remaining work behind a queue before whole-batch acknowledgement fits it.
rubricReasons.accuracy: The reread unit accepts 202, gives the 30-second wait and whole-batch retry semantics; the queue units support successful durable acceptance followed by separate processing.
rubricReasons.scenarioCompleteness: The elapsed 12 seconds, two completed durable jobs, remaining minute, two-second durable enqueue and available worker make the processing and reliability boundaries explicit.
rubricReasons.answerUniqueness: Synchronous completion reaches about 72 seconds, the successful enqueue response about 14, and 503 asks for whole-batch replay. Only b meets all three supplied constraints.
rubricReasons.distractorPlausibility: Synchronous completion and retry-on-failure are real plans, but the timing and no-requested-replay constraints strongly rule them out here.
rubricReasons.distractorEvidence: The actual delivery unit directly supports a successful in-window synchronous response and a 503 whole-batch retry when acceptance fails.
rubricReasons.documentationStrength: The complete delivery and Service Bus units jointly cover status codes, acknowledgement granularity, response timing, queued ownership and the absence of exactly-once guarantees.
rubricReasons.citationSpecificity: All three references are exact substantive training units linked by their current-course modules; the course itself supplies no technical support and no withdrawn article is used.
rubricReasons.difficultyAuthenticity: Intermediate architecture-design is defensible but easy. The task applies acknowledgement and durable responsibility to partial batch state; supplied arithmetic and architecture do not merit full difficulty realism or Advanced credit.
rubricReasons.explanationQuality: The explanation requires successful durable acceptance before 202 and explicitly withdraws that premise if enqueue fails, avoiding an unsafe fire-and-forget interpretation.
rubricReasons.originality: The partial-batch framing is original but applies a conventional asynchronous acceptance design. It is a revision of r-i-006, not another current fact beside v1.
rubricReasons.clarityAccessibility: Completed versus remaining jobs, webhook response and queue worker are consistently distinguished. The pronoun warning has a single clear webhook/batch referent.
